taxonomy:
# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop through cells, constrained by black/white circle rules
- **Slitherlink** – Loop on grid edges/dots, constrained by number clues
- **Mid-loop** – Loop through cells, black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directed loop with wind constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop through rooms, alternating between moon/sun symbols
- **Suraromu** – Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in order
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop through cells, with straight/turn constraints per region based on white circles; avoids black circles

#### A2. Loop with Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop plus placement of black cells, with directional number clues

#### A3. Path/Connection Drawing
- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect island nodes with bridges (1 or 2), forming a connected network

---

### B. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver colors certain cells black (or leaves them white).

#### B1. Shading with Number Clues (counting adjacent/nearby black cells)
- **Kurotto** – Numbers in circles indicate sum of contiguous black cell groups touching the circle
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers indicate size of white islands; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers indicate count of visible white cells in four directions
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs; numbers on black cells count adjacent bulbs; all white cells illuminated, no bulb-to-bulb visibility
- **Usowan** – Numbers count adjacent black cells, but exactly one number per room is wrong

#### B2. Shading with Regional Constraints
- **Heyawake** – Numbers indicate black cell count per room; no horizontal/vertical white line spans 3+ rooms; black cells non-adjacent; white cells connected
- **Norinori** – Exactly two black cells per region, each black cell part of a domino
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white "promontories" (one white neighbor); numbers indicate length of white line; no 2×2 of either color
- **Nurimeizu** – Rooms entirely black or white; creates maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles not
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two shaded blocks of equal size; all shaded cells connected; no 2×2 shading
- **LITS** – Place one tetromino per region; same-shape tetrominoes non-adjacent; all shaded connected; no 2×2
- **Sto-stone** – Numbers indicate black cell count per room; black cells don't connect across rooms; when "dropped" they fill bottom half

#### B3. Shading to Form Geometric Shapes
- **Choco Banana** – Black cell groups must form rectangles/squares; white cell groups must not form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate area size
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares; numbers count adjacent triangles
- **Tilepaint** – Entire tiles colored or not; diagonal-cell numbers indicate black cell counts in row/column segments

#### B4. Shading by Elimination
- **Hitori** – Shade duplicate numbers so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells non-adjacent; white cells connected

---

### C. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### C1. Region-Based Number Fill
- **Fillomino** – Fill grid with numbers; contiguous same-number groups have size equal to that number; same-sized blocks non-adjacent
- **Ripple Effect** – Each room gets consecutive numbers 1 to N; same numbers in a row/column must be spaced apart by at least that number
- **Makaro** – Each room gets 1 to N; arrows in black cells point to the largest neighbor; same numbers can't be adjacent across rooms
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box

#### C2. Number Placement from a List
- **Nansuke** – Fill blank cells using numbers from a provided list, forming valid multi-digit entries

#### C3. Symbol Placement
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference in counts; runs of — limited vertically, runs of | limited horizontally

---

### D. Grid Division/Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.

#### D1. Division into Rectangles
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area

#### D2. Division into Polyominoes/Specific Shapes
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentominoes; numbers indicate count of block boundary edges around that cell
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends, numbers indicate block size
- **Double Choco** – Divide grid so each block has matching white and gray sub-regions of identical shape

#### D3. Division with Evolving Shapes
- **Evolomino** – Place square markers forming blocks along arrows; each successive block adds one square to the previous shape

---

### E. Object Placement/Movement
Puzzles where the solver places or moves discrete objects.

#### E1. Placement of Objects
- **Akari** (also in B1) – Place light bulbs in white cells
- **Hebi** – Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells with visibility and adjacency constraints

#### E2. Movement of Objects
- **Satogaeri** – Move circles within countries so each country has exactly one; numbers indicate distance moved; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – Move circles into gray areas via straight arrows; numbers in gray areas equal sum of entering circle values

---

### F. Block/Chain Formation
Puzzles focused on forming and connecting groups of cells.

- **Chained Block** – Mark cells as black to form blocks; each block contains one number (its size) or "?"; all blocks connected via corner-touching chains; no duplicate block shape/size within a chain

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism

### Adjacency/Visibility Constraints
- Akari, Kurodoko, Hebi, Shakashaka, Kurotto, Usowan

### Connectivity Constraints (white/black cells must be connected or non-adjacent)
- Heyawake, Hitori, Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, LITS, Yajilin, Usowan

### No 2×2 Constraint
- Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, LITS, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone

### Regional/Room Constraints
- Heyawake, Norinori, Double Choco, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Five Cells

### Directional/Arrow Constraints
- Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Nagareru, Sashigane, Evolomino, Yosenabe

### Gravity/Physical Simulation
- Sto-stone (dropping stones)

---

## III. By Grid Element Types

| Element | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Numbered black cells** | Akari, Shakashaka, Hebi, Yajilin |
| **Circled numbers** | Hashiwokakero, Kurotto, Kurodoko, Satogaeri, Nurimisaki, Suraromu, Yosenabe |
| **Black/white circle markers** | Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop |
| **Bold-line rooms/regions** | Heyawake, Norinori, Double Choco, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Five Cells, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Suraromu, Usowan, Sto-stone |
| **Dotted grid lines** | Slitherlink, Double Choco, Sashigane |
| **Arrows** | Makaro, Hebi, Sashigane, Evolomino, Nagareru, Yajilin, Yosenabe |
| **Pre-filled numbers** | Sudoku, Fillomino, Hitori, Nansuke, Ripple Effect |
| **Moon/Sun symbols** | Moon-or-Sun |
| **Gates (dotted lines between cells)** | Suraromu |
| **Colored (gray/white) cell regions** | Double Choco, Sto-stone |
| **Diagonal clue cells** | Tilepaint |
